newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Union Bancaire Privee net profits up 4.3 pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: Union Bancaire Privee net profits up 4.3 pct in 96.

text.p: Swiss private bank Union Bancaire Privee said on Tuesday its net profits rose 4.3 percent to 161.3 million Swiss francs in 1996 from a year ago.

In a rare announcement on financial results in Switzerland's secretive private banking hub, the Geneva-based bank said in a statement that its consolidated balance sheet grew 6.1 percent to 13.41 billion Swiss francs.

Union Bancaire Privee's consolidated income rose 11 percent to 449 million Swiss francs from a year ago, but the rise in expenditure was higher at 23.9 percent to 205.7 million Swiss francs because of an increase in investments.

The bank said 1996 was marked by expansion abroad and restructuring and consolidation at home. Investments abroad included the launch of an asset management operation in New York and the purchase of a stake in Brazil's Banco Excel Economico.
The statement gave no other details. The bank does not publish the volume of assets it manages.
Swiss private bankers estimate that assets under management in the industry grew by 15 percent in 1996, which they say was a good year in terms of return on investments and new cash flows.

There are no official statistics on the Swiss private banking industry, but a recent survey by Credit Swiss First Boston bank put the volume of private assets under management in Switzerland at some $1.8 trillion.
